title: Print Generator Running Totals
description: Read one line of comma-separated integers. Use a generator to produce the cumulative total after each value, then print the totals separated by spaces. Ignore empty input. The generator should yield values as it goes rather than build a second list.
starterCode: # Read the comma-separated integers, then print their cumulative totals
referenceSolution:
def running_totals(values):
    total = 0
    for value in values:
        total += value
        yield total

raw = input().strip()
values = [int(part.strip()) for part in raw.split(",") if part.strip()]
print(" ".join(str(value) for value in running_totals(values)))

solution.code:
def running_totals(values):
    total = 0
    for value in values:
        total += value
        yield total

raw = input().strip()
values = [int(part.strip()) for part in raw.split(",") if part.strip()]
print(" ".join(str(value) for value in running_totals(values)))
solution.explanation: Read the comma-separated numbers, feed them through a generator that keeps a running total, and print each yielded value. The generator produces values one at a time while preserving the cumulative state. Empty input becomes an empty sequence, so the program prints a blank line.

wrongSolutions:
raw = input().strip()
values = [int(part) for part in raw.split(",")]
print(" ".join(str(value) for value in values))

tests.hint: Handle an empty input line without creating numbers.
The first yielded total equals the first value.
Each output keeps the sum from prior values.
Negative values adjust the running total.
Zero values still yield a total at each step.
Whitespace around comma-separated integers is allowed.
The running total can return to zero.
Repeated values produce one total per input.
Several decreases should keep the sequence state.
A longer input should still yield every cumulative total in order.
